narrative:
The model predicts an 88% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out as the most influential in this decision. First, your overall years of experience pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. With 6-10 years total, you sit in a group where many employees start exploring new opportunities outside their current role. Second, having received other job offers while working here added significant weight toward predicting you would leave. Third, your 1-5 years in this specific organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction, as this tenure range often aligns with employees who feel ready for a change.

These elements together created a clear pattern the model recognizes from past cases: experienced professionals who are being approached by other employers tend to move on. Although you have medical coverage, feel recognized at work, and report general job satisfaction, the combination of your broader experience level, external opportunities, and time already spent here outweighed those positives.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or adjusted responsibilities. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still matches your long-term goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook. (248 words)
